messages:
alex: Quick preflight question — before I spin a full batch8 regression, can someone confirm the minimal nsys + torch.profiler sequence we prefer for diagnosing KV warmup/regression? want to keep traces small.
maya: short answer: 30s nsys for whole-process timeline + 5-10 iters of torch.profiler around the hot loop. capture NVTX and CUDA in nsys and function-level stack in torchprof.
runtime-bot: Reminder: upload artifacts to s3://redwood-profiling/2765432100 and include a brief run_meta.txt (:white_check_mark:)
chris: +1 to maya. My usual smoke sequence:

```
# nsys warmup (captures cuda + nvtx)
NSYS_OUT=/tmp/nsys_2765432100
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=${NSYS_OUT} --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=stop \
  --duration=30 --sample=none --kill=none -- python -u run_infer.py --model rlm-test

# then lightweight torch.profiler around 8 iters
python -c "from torch.profiler import profile, record_function, ProfilerActivity; ..."
```

chris: attach both .qdrep (nsys) and the profiler .json/.txt
sophie: two extras — set SEQ_LEN to a realistic target (e.g., 1024) and ensure KV_PREFILL=64 for the warmup workload so we exercise the cache path.

maya: also include a short command that reproduces the client request rate (e.g., --concurrency 4 --batch-size 1) so we hit the batching logic.

alex: got it. any redaction guidance? dont want keys or sample payloads in traces.
sophie: redact env vars and request payloads; truncate token texts in the profiler metadata. if you need a helper script, use tools/prof/scrub_artifact.sh and set --strip-requests.

alex: perfect — i'll run the smoke now and upload links here. i'll ping if i need a deeper trace capture.
maya: thanks — if the smoke shows a KV miss spike, tag @chris and we'll coordinate a 1-hr bisect slot.
chris: available after 14:00 PT today.
runtime-bot: Artifact checklist: nsys .qdrep, torchprof .json, run_meta.txt (cmdline + env diff), scrubbed_request_sample.txt
alex: uploading in ~15m. thx everyone :pray:
